fatal_errors: The proposed WC-Co-Ni-Fe cemented carbide is fundamentally different from the target MgAlTiVFeCo lightweight multi-principal-element alloy.
The proposed 1450 °C processing window conflicts with the target 800–1000 °C window and would aggravate magnesium volatilization in the intended alloy.
The cited study used low-pressure argon sintering and does not substantiate the proposed SPS result.
No cited evidence supports improved aqueous corrosion resistance, chloride-blocking passivation, or performance in 3.5 wt% NaCl.
No cited evidence supports oxidation resistance above 1000 °C or the proposed protective Ni/Fe-rich oxide scale.
The hypothesis misses the target oxide barrier phases, parabolic biphasic oxidation kinetics, and corrosion-potential/current-density mechanism.
The proposed system is a dense WC-based composite rather than a credible lightweight alloy.
explanation: The response supplies a coherent but largely unrelated carbide hypothesis. It shares ball milling and nominal SPS with the target, but changes the material class, composition, phase constitution, temperature regime, structural mediator, and environmental-resistance mechanism. E1 supports an optimum of 5.46 wt% C and 1450 °C for low-pressure-sintered WC-10CoNiFe, including grain refinement and mechanical properties, but it does not support SPS, oxidation, or corrosion claims. It also reports lower hardness and flexural strength than optimized WC-10Co, weakening the asserted broad property advantage. The proposed experiment can test grain refinement and oxidation behavior, but it omits aqueous corrosion measurements and does not discriminate the target passive-film and oxide-barrier mechanism.
